Name: Layered Left-to-Right
Keywords: layered; left-to-right; tiered; request-flow; client-to-db; horizontal-flow; ltr
Flow Direction: left-to-right; strict horizontal tiers (client to gateway to service to storage)
When to Use: request/response flows; typical 3-5 tier web architectures; C4 container diagrams
When NOT: cyclic or peer-to-peer topologies; more than 6 tiers (becomes too wide); mobile-narrow viewports
Spacing Rules: column gap 220px; row gap 120px; node 160x80; label offset 12px; tier header offset 24px above first node
Grouping Rule: group nodes into vertical tier columns by architectural role (client/gateway/compute/storage); same-tier nodes share a column x-coordinate

Name: Layered Top-to-Bottom
Keywords: layered; top-to-bottom; vertical-flow; tiered; portrait; ttb; stacked-tiers
When to Use: portrait-oriented docs; mobile-friendly embeds; presentation slides with limited width
When NOT: wide multi-branch flows better suited to horizontal space; diagrams with many parallel branches per tier
Spacing Rules: row gap 160px; column gap 200px; node 160x80; label offset 12px; tier header offset 16px left of first node
Grouping Rule: group nodes into horizontal tier rows by architectural role; same-tier nodes share a row y-coordinate

Name: Clustered Domains
Keywords: clustered; domain-driven; bounded-context; grouped; microservices; ownership; ddd; swimlane; team; per-team
Flow Direction: no single global direction; local flow within each cluster, cross-cluster edges as needed
When to Use: microservices grouped by bounded context or team ownership; domain-driven design overviews
When NOT: single linear request path; fewer than 2 distinct domains; strict sequence diagrams
Spacing Rules: cluster padding 32px; inter-cluster gap 260px; intra-cluster node gap 100px; node 160x80; cluster label offset 16px above cluster border
Grouping Rule: draw a rounded-rectangle boundary per domain cluster with a domain-name label at top-left; nodes belonging to a domain sit fully inside its boundary; cross-domain edges cross cluster borders and are drawn with a distinct dashed style

Name: Hub and Spoke
Keywords: hub-spoke; central-gateway; star-topology; fanout; api-gateway-pattern; radial
Flow Direction: radial outward from one central hub node to N spoke nodes
When to Use: API gateway or event-bus fanning out to many services; central orchestrator patterns
When NOT: peer-to-peer meshes with no true center; deep multi-hop chains
Spacing Rules: spoke node 160x80 (the one shipped node box); hub node 200x100 = that same box scaled 1.25x uniformly via the scale-wrapper mechanism documented in templates/snippets/node-shapes.html -- the hub is larger on purpose because it is the subject of the diagram; spoke radius = the larger of 360px and 100px / sin(180deg / N) which keeps >=40px clearance between adjacent spokes at any N in the sweet spot; minimum angular gap 24deg between spokes; edge label offset 10px perpendicular from the spoke midpoint -- push the radius out when a label is wider than radius minus 130px
Grouping Rule: single hub node at layout center; spokes distributed evenly around a circle at fixed radius, angle = 360/N * index; group spokes by type (e.g. all data stores on one arc segment) when types exist

Name: Swimlane
Keywords: swimlane; sequence-diagram; lanes; actor-lanes; cross-functional; process-flow
Flow Direction: left-to-right time progression across vertical actor lanes
When to Use: sequence flows across multiple actors or systems; cross-functional process diagrams; auth flows
When NOT: diagrams without a clear actor/participant set; static topology with no temporal ordering
Spacing Rules: lane height 140px; lane label column width 200px; step column gap 130px; node 160x80 (leaves 60px of clear lane between adjacent lanes); message arrow vertical offset 8px per concurrent message
Grouping Rule: one horizontal lane per actor/participant, lane order fixed top-to-bottom by call sequence; each step is a vertical timestamp column shared across all lanes

Name: Ring / Peer Network
Keywords: ring; peer-to-peer; consistent-hashing; hash-ring; gossip; distributed-hash-table; p2p; sharding
Flow Direction: circular, no start or end; edges drawn as ring segments or chords between peer nodes
When to Use: consistent-hashing rings; gossip protocols; peer-to-peer replication topologies; distributed hash tables
When NOT: hierarchical or directional flows; client-server request paths; fewer than 3 peers
Spacing Rules: ring radius = the larger of 300px and 100px / sin(180deg / N) which keeps >=40px clearance between adjacent peers at any N in the sweet spot; node 160x80 centred on the ring at angle = 360/N * index; hash-range arc stroke-width 14px; virtual-node tick mark length 8px
Grouping Rule: peers placed evenly around the ring by angle; the ring circumference is segmented into colored hash-range arcs, one per owning node, with partition-boundary tick marks at each arc join; virtual nodes for a physical peer render as smaller secondary tick marks in that peer's color; failover and replica edges draw as chords crossing the ring interior

Name: Tree Hierarchy
Keywords: tree; hierarchy; parent-child; org-chart; dag; nested; recursive-structure
Flow Direction: top-down (root at top) or left-to-right (root at left), single parent per child
When to Use: organizational hierarchies; nested component breakdowns; recursive workflow orchestration trees
When NOT: graphs with multiple parents per node (use clustered-domains instead); cyclic dependencies
Spacing Rules: level gap (vertical edge-to-edge) 140px; sibling gap (horizontal edge-to-edge) 60px; node 160x80; subtree centering offset computed as average of children x; label offset 10px
Grouping Rule: each node positioned directly below (or right of) its parent; sibling subtrees are spaced to avoid overlap and the parent is horizontally centered over its children's midpoint

Name: Timeline Sequence
Keywords: timeline; sequence; chronological; step-by-step; batch-schedule; event-timeline; linear-history; interaction; dialogue; communication; over-time
Flow Direction: single horizontal (or vertical) axis progressing strictly by time/step order
When to Use: batch job schedules; deployment rollout steps; incident timelines; state-machine transition history
When NOT: concurrent multi-actor interactions (use swimlane); non-temporal structural diagrams
Spacing Rules: axis tick gap 150px; event marker 40px diameter; node/event card 160x80 offset 60px above or below the axis alternating (same-side cards then sit 300px apart -- 140px of clear space at 160px card width); label offset 8px
Grouping Rule: events placed along a single axis in strict chronological order; alternate event cards above/below the axis to avoid label overlap; concurrent events at the same timestamp stack vertically at that axis position

Name: Geo Map (Abstract)
Keywords: geo-map; multi-region; geographic; cdn-edge; latency-map; global-distribution; region-topology
Flow Direction: no single direction; cross-region edges labeled with latency, replica/failover arrows point toward the active or recovery region
When to Use: multi-region deployments; CDN edge routing; geo-routing/DNS failover; DDoS mitigation edge maps
When NOT: single-region architectures; diagrams needing real-world geographic precision; fewer than 2 regions
Spacing Rules: region cluster 480x430 rounded rect (holds the stated 6 nodes as 2 columns x 3 rows: 32px padding + 160 + 60 + 160 = 444 wide and 3x80 + 2x60 + 64 = 424 tall); inter-region gap 280px; intra-region node gap 60px; node 160x80; latency-label offset 14px at edge midpoint; region pseudo-position by cardinal layout (NA left, EU center, APAC right)
Grouping Rule: each region is a rounded-cluster boundary labeled with region code (e.g. us-east-1); regions arranged in a pseudo-geographic layout, not to real map scale, just relative cardinal placement; inter-region edges carry a latency label (e.g. 85ms) at their midpoint; replica-sync and failover-reroute edges drawn as bold dashed arrows crossing region boundaries, colored distinctly from normal traffic edges

Name: Split Compare
Keywords: split compare; side by side; before after; versus; comparison panes; ab compare; stacked panes; top bottom compare
Flow Direction: per-pane independent; panes ordered by argument (worse to better or before to after); the PANE AXIS is perpendicular to the panes own internal flow axis
When to Use: comparing 2-6 solutions to ONE problem where the delta is the message; pattern-level contrasts such as with vs without pubsub
When NOT: more than 6 variants; panes needing more than 8 components (wrong altitude -- compare the pattern not the full system); unrelated systems that share no components
Spacing Rules: pane gutter >=80px plus 1px rule line; shared title band; verdict chip zone per pane; ORIENTATION -- 2 panes split the canvas axis the per-pane flow does NOT use: horizontal per-pane flow (protocol timelines; left-to-right hop chains) stacks panes TOP/BOTTOM; vertical per-pane flow (a request falling through layers) puts them SIDE-BY-SIDE; side-by-side is only the default because most panes flow downward; 3-4 panes grid 2x2; 5-6 panes grid 2x3 landscape or 3x2 vertical
Grouping Rule: identical components pinned to identical relative positions across panes; in a stacked pair that pinning is a shared x so the reader diffs straight down a column; delta components take the accent; each pane fully self-contained with no cross-pane edges

Name: Progressive Tiers
Keywords: progressive tiers; load tiers; growth stages; scale thresholds; ccu evolution; architecture evolution
Flow Direction: tier bands in load order low to high; each tier internally layered
When to Use: narrating ONE system across load thresholds (for example 0 to 500K CCU); each tier boundary is an architecture break point -- the thing that broke -- never an arithmetic split of the range
When NOT: more than 5 tiers; stories where the architecture never changes (annotate one diagram instead); comparing different systems (use split-compare)
Spacing Rules: tier band gutter >=120px plus a transition caption zone between bands; HARD GATE: every tier fits one camera frame at k_read; the overview zoom may be far out -- legibility is judged per tier
Grouping Rule: components alive across tiers keep shape color and relative position; each tier's NEW components take the accent; retired components never reappear; the transition caption names what broke and what was added
